title: Launch risk coordination: safe-stop triggers, stakeholder comms, and rollback validation runbook
creator: Asha Raman
description: Purpose: Create a runnable, low-friction runbook and stakeholder communication bundle for the upcoming runtime-1.22 launch. Focus areas: (1) define technical safe-stop triggers that will automatically or manually halt rollout; (2) produce concise incident and rollback comms tailored for engineering, customers, sales, and legal; (3) document step-by-step rollback and post-rollback validation so on-call and SRE teams can confidently revert and confirm system health. This ticket coordinates cross-team review and sign-off.
updates: 2025-03-01: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, Console, Legal, and Customer Success. Agreed to use three-tier stop logic (auto, manual immediate, manual conditional). Assigned owners for each comm template.

2025-03-02: Drafted safe-stop thresholds (see 'safe_stop_triggers'). Shared preliminary templates in #launch-ops for feedback. Noted requirement from Legal to include 'investigating' wording for external-facing messages.
2025-03-03: SRE: load testing produced a P99 latency spike at 420ms baseline with KV-cache miss. Adjusted thresholds. Runtime eng raised a kernel fallback risk — added as a blocker candidate.

2025-03-04: PM reviewed comm templates with CS and Sales; updated customer-facing template to include remediation ETA placeholder and link to status.redwood.ai. Preparing canary gating checklist and preflight runbook additions.
Action items: Diego to finalize runbook steps and link GH PRs; Lila (SRE) to validate automated abort hook in staging by 2025-03-07; Legal to sign off on external wording by 2025-03-05.
safe_stop_triggers: AUTO-ABORT: sustained 5xx rate >= 3% cluster-wide for 3 continuous minutes during canary (automated hook)
AUTO-ABORT: p99 latency increase > 2x baseline for 10 minutes on production-serving nodes
MANUAL-IMMEDIATE: catastrophic error flood (>=10% request failures) or data corruption alerts — on-call must stop rollout immediately
MANUAL-CONDITIONAL: error rate between 1% and 3% for >10 minutes OR latency p99 degradation 1.5x baseline for >15 minutes — requires incident lead review before continuing
release_blockers: Blocking: runtime kernel fallback observed in canary that causes cache invalidation (ENG-81234). Until patch merged, restrict canary to 5% traffic.
High: missing automated abort hook in staging for dedicated pools (SRE-4391). Must be validated before ramp beyond 10%.
Medium: incomplete telemetry dashboard per-route breakdown in Console (PM-82311) — mitigated by temporary dashboard link in comms.
rollback_steps: Step 1: Announce immediate rollback intent in #launch-ops and trigger P0 channel. Ping on-call SRE and runtime leads.
Step 2: Use rollout console to revert deployment to previous pinned model/version. Confirm command returns successful state change.
Step 3: Drain traffic from new variant with graceful connection close; verify no in-flight requests are orphaned.
Step 4: Disable autoscaling changes applied during rollout window to avoid capacity thrash.
Step 5: Re-enable previous traffic weights and confirm token-level latency and error metrics return to baseline in 5 minutes windows for 3 consecutive windows.
Step 6: Open incident in PagerDuty and attach rollback log, PR links, and timeline. Assign incident lead and set severity.
Step 7: Communicate rollback completion across stakeholders using templates; follow post-rollback validation checklist.
post_rollback_validation: Confirm global p95/p99 latency back within 10% of pre-launch baseline for 30 minutes
Verify 5xx and 4xx error rates returned to baseline and no spike of client-side retries observed
Run end-to-end smoke tests for sample tenants (CS-owned) and validate correctness of outputs for saved prompts
Check KV cache hit-rate for affected models hasn't regressed more than 5% versus baseline
Ensure logs and traces for the rollback window are archived to the incident folder and accessible to owners
incident_comms_templates: Engineering (internal): 'We are initiating a rollback for runtime-1.22 due to [TRIGGER]. Actions taken: revert to vX.Y, drain variant, and start post-rollback validation. Owners: @Diego_Morales (PM), @LilaChen-SRE. Timeline: ETA 20–30 minutes. See incident doc: {incident-link}.'

Customer (outbound): 'We are aware of an issue affecting inference latency/availability for a subset of customers and are rolling back a recent platform update while we investigate. We expect services to return to normal within 30–60 minutes; we will send an update at 1 hour and when resolved. For urgent needs, contact your account team or support@redwood.ai. Status page: {status-link}.'

Sales/Customer Success (internal): 'Heads-up: we rolled back runtime-1.22 for safety. Please avoid proactive outreach until the incident is classified. If customers reach out, use the outbound template and escalate priority accounts to CS-leads.'
Legal/Compliance (internal): 'Logged incident: potential impact on regulated workloads. Preserve logs and avoid sharing PII in comms. Legal will review external statements before public posting.'

CS: requested customer template include account-specific contact placeholder; updated template accordingly.
Legal: approved external wording with minor edits; required copy to include status page and remediation ETA placeholders.
